notes:
Summary: OmniThread runs a SaaS support platform used by ~600 mid-market customers. Primary product is an in-app support console + knowledge base. They want to add an always-on RAG layer for KB answers: embeddings for retrieval + lightweight reranking for precision. Target: moderate index (~1.5-3M passages), very high QPS at peak (200-600 qps), and strict tail latency SLOs (p90 end-to-end < 200ms for user-facing retrieval+rerank). Cost sensitive — current ops budget estimates want < $0.02 per query end-to-end if possible.

Requirements (from discovery calls):
- Workload: real-time KB retrieval for customer-facing chat and agent assist. Mix of short queries + contextual chat.
- Indexing: 1.5M passages today, expect 3M within 12 months. Frequent increments (daily delta indexing).
- Throughput: average 120 qps, peak 400-600 qps during enterprise bursts.
- Latency: p50 < 60ms (retrieval), p90 end-to-end (retrieve + embed + rerank) < 200ms.
- Models: prefer off-the-shelf dense embeddings (512-1024 dim) + a small cross-encoder reranker for top-10. Open to Redwood curated models.
- Routing/fallbacks: want automatic fallback to cheaper model when cost pressure or regional capacity constraints occur.
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML for admin console, audit logs for queries, EU residency for EU customers (must support region pinning).
- Operational: need token-level cost visibility, per-route latency dashboards, alerting on query cost overruns.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2025-10-03: initial inbound trial sign-up; AE assigned (Maya P.).
- 2025-11-12: discovery call — mapped current architecture (Elasticsearch + custom embeddings store). Recorded (ff-20251112-discovery).
- 2026-01-07: technical deep-dive w/SE (Daniel K.) — explored embedding dims, incremental indexing cadence.
- 2026-02-11: POC kickoff — Redwood hosted API POC configured in us-east and eu-west regions. Drive: POC pricing + security questionnaire shared.
- 2026-02-18: Load test (simulated 500 qps) run against retrieval path only. Results: retrieval p95 ~ 75ms; reranker single-threaded p95 ~ 180ms when colocated — indicates need for optimized batching or smaller reranker.
- 2026-03-02: Redwood Optimize suggestions delivered: prefix caching, compressing vectors to 768 dim, and recommend reranker quantization. Cost impact estimate attached.
- 2026-03-09: Sync with engineering (internal) — want updated cost per query with recommended optimizations.

POC details / metrics observed:
- Index: 1.8M passages; embedding dim 1024 baseline.
- Retrieval: ANN vector search latency p50 28ms, p95 72ms (eu-west deployed).
- Reranking: cross-encoder (base) p50 90ms for rank-10, p95 220ms unless batched; batch-friendly reranker reduced p95 to ~120ms in tests.
- Cost: raw hosted API estimate (baseline models) ~ $0.045 per query; with suggested optimizations estimate drops to $0.018 per query.

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "We need consistently snappy answers for customers — long tails kill CSAT."
- "If we can hit ~15-20ms extra for reranking, we can live with it; beyond that it's too slow."

Open questions for procurement:
- Confirm EU data residency SLA and how long audit logs retained by default.
- Clarify pricing tiers for high-QPS committed blocks vs pure pay-as-you-go.
- Will Redwood provide a pre-baked lightweight reranker (quantized) as part of Optimize?

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-15: Cost/latency tuning call with SE + pricing (Maya, Daniel, OmniThread infra lead).
- Provide final POC report with tuned numbers and recommended model profiles (by 2026-03-18).
- Procurement to decide on 12-month reserved commit vs burstable hosted plan (target decision: 2026-04).

Suggested AE playbook notes:
- Emphasize hosted API fast time-to-value and Optimize recommendations that hit target cost.
- Prepare a clear comparison sheet vs Pinecone + external reranker (cost + latency + ops overhead).
- Keep security pack (SOC2, SSO, EU residency) easily accessible — procurement will escalate quickly.

Internal Redwood flags:
- High upside ARR if they commit to reserved blocks given sustained QPS.
- Technical complexity: daily incremental indexing + bursty QPS requires good autoscaling and cache policies.

short_summary: Mid-market SaaS (OmniThread) evaluating Redwood hosted API for KB RAG: moderate index (1.5-3M), high QPS (200-600), p90 E2E <200ms, cost target < $0.02/query. POC shows retrieval fast; reranker needs batching/quantization to meet SLOs. Procurement Q2 decision.
